package.title: Tempo.Blazor
package.description: Comprehensive Blazor component library with 100+ components. Supports WebAssembly, Server, and InteractiveAuto render modes. Multi-targets .NET 8/9/10. Includes multilingual support (EN/CS), CSS variable theming, and dark mode. Optional FluentValidation integration is available through Tempo.Blazor.FluentValidation.

gettingStarted.title: Getting Started with Tempo.Blazor
gettingStarted.overview: Tempo.Blazor is a comprehensive Blazor WebAssembly component library providing 100+ UI components for building modern web applications. It includes inputs, forms, data tables, pickers, charts, layout, navigation, feedback, workflow designer, scheduler, and more. All components use the Tm prefix (e.g., TmButton, TmDataTable).
gettingStarted.platform: Blazor WebAssembly, Blazor Server, and InteractiveAuto (hybrid rendering)

renderModes.description: Tempo.Blazor supports all Blazor render modes.

modes.name: InteractiveWebAssembly
modes.description: Full client-side rendering in the browser via WebAssembly.

modes.name: InteractiveServer
modes.description: Server-side rendering with SignalR connection for interactivity.

modes.name: InteractiveAuto
modes.description: Starts with Server rendering, switches to WebAssembly once downloaded. Recommended for best UX.

renderModes.notes: Components with JS interop (dashboard, workflow designer, rich editor, scheduler, PDF viewer, diagram editor, color picker, file manager, Gantt, Notion editor, document editor, signing, spreadsheet, wireframe designer, and email variable insertion) gracefully degrade during prerendering and activate once the client-side runtime is available.

cssFramework.description: Tempo.Blazor uses its own standalone CSS framework based on CSS custom properties (design tokens). No external CSS framework (like Bootstrap or Tailwind) is required. The library ships a single tempo-blazor.bundled.css file that includes all component styles, design tokens, base resets, and animations.
cssFramework.architecture: The CSS is organized as: tokens (design variables) → base resets → component styles. Each component uses BEM-like class naming with the tm- prefix (e.g., tm-btn, tm-data-table, tm-modal__header).

darkMode.description: Dark mode is supported via CSS custom property overrides. Activate by adding data-theme="dark" attribute or .tm-dark class to a parent element (typically <html> or <body>).
darkMode.themeService: Use the ThemeService (registered via DI) to toggle themes programmatically.

designTokens.description: All visual properties are controlled via CSS custom properties (--tm-*). Override these to customize the look and feel without modifying component CSS.

colorPrimary.description: Primary brand color palette (blue by default)

typography.description: Font families, sizes, weights, and line heights

tokens.--tm-font-mono: ui-monospace, 'Cascadia Code', 'Source Code Pro', Menlo, monospace

customization.description: Override design tokens in your app CSS to customize the theme globally.

localization.description: Tempo.Blazor supports localization via the ITmLocalizer interface (namespace Tempo.Blazor.Localization, defined in Tempo.Blazor.Abstractions). All built-in component UI strings (button labels, tooltips, placeholders, validation messages, aria-labels, etc.) go through this interface. The library ships with 500+ localization keys covering all components.

architecture.interface: ITmLocalizer — two indexer overloads: this[string key] for simple lookups, this[string key, params object[] arguments] for formatted strings (e.g. Loc["TmImageGallery_Counter", 5, 20] → "5 of 20").
architecture.defaultImplementation: DefaultTmLocalizer (internal) — backed by IStringLocalizer<TmResources> using embedded .resx files (TmResources.resx for English, TmResources.cs.resx for Czech).
architecture.injection: All components get the localizer via @inject ITmLocalizer Loc in the library's _Imports.razor. Components then use Loc["KeyName"] in markup and code.
architecture.registration: AddTempoBlazor() registers: (1) ITmLocalizer as Singleton (stateless, thread-safe, backed by .resx), (2) ThemeService as Scoped (per-circuit in Server, per-tab in WASM), (3) ToastService as Scoped (per-circuit in Server, per-tab in WASM). Uses TryAdd* so your custom registrations take precedence if registered AFTER AddTempoBlazor().

localization.keyNamingConvention: Keys follow the pattern Tm[ComponentName]_[Action/State]. Shared keys use Tm_ prefix (e.g. Tm_Save, Tm_Cancel, Tm_Loading). Component-specific keys include the component name (e.g. TmDataTable_NoResults, TmRichEditor_Bold, TmFilterBuilder_Contains).

keyCategories.shared: Tm_Loading, Tm_Close, Tm_Cancel, Tm_Save, Tm_Delete, Tm_Confirm, Tm_NoResults, Tm_Error, Tm_Retry, Tm_Search, Tm_Clear, Tm_Select, Tm_SelectAll, Tm_DeselectAll, Tm_Edit, Tm_Add, Tm_Remove, Tm_Apply, Tm_Reset, Tm_Previous, Tm_Next, Tm_Download, Tm_Upload, Tm_Create, Tm_Optional, Tm_Required, Tm_Yes, Tm_No
keyCategories.dataTable: TmDataTable_NoResults, TmDataTable_Loading, TmDataTable_PageSize, TmDataTable_SearchPlaceholder, TmDataTable_ShowingItems, TmDataTable_SelectAll, TmDataTable_DeselectAll, TmDataTable_BulkActions, TmDataTable_ExpandAll, TmDataTable_CollapseAll, TmDataTable_GroupDropPlaceholder
keyCategories.richEditor: TmRichEditor_Bold, TmRichEditor_Italic, TmRichEditor_Underline, TmRichEditor_Undo, TmRichEditor_Redo, TmRichEditor_InsertLink, TmRichEditor_InsertImage, TmRichEditor_InsertTable, etc. (56 keys total)
keyCategories.filterBuilder: TmFilterBuilder_Equals, TmFilterBuilder_NotEquals, TmFilterBuilder_Contains, TmFilterBuilder_StartsWith, TmFilterBuilder_Between, TmFilterBuilder_GreaterThan, TmFilterBuilder_LessThan, TmFilterBuilder_In, TmFilterBuilder_NotIn, etc.
keyCategories.pickers: TmDatePicker_Today, TmDatePicker_Clear, TmTimePicker_Hours, TmTimePicker_Minutes, TmDateRangePicker_LastWeek, TmDateRangePicker_LastMonth, TmDateRangePicker_ThisYear, etc.
keyCategories.other: TmAlert_Dismiss, TmButton_Loading, TmSearchInput_Placeholder, TmNotificationBell_*, TmViewManager_*, TmDashboard_*, TmPasswordStrength_*, TmActivity_*, TmTimeline_*, etc.

switchLanguage.description: Set the culture in Program.cs before builder.Build(). This makes IStringLocalizer pick the correct .resx file automatically.

customLocalizer.description: To fully replace all component strings (e.g. for a language not shipped with the library), implement ITmLocalizer and register it AFTER AddTempoBlazor(). The TryAddSingleton in AddTempoBlazor() will be skipped if your registration comes first.

partialOverride.description: To override only specific keys while keeping the rest from the built-in resources, create a decorator that falls back to the default implementation.

addNewLanguage.description: To add a new language (e.g. German), implement ITmLocalizer with all keys translated. You can export the English .resx keys as a reference. Since DefaultTmLocalizer is internal, a full custom implementation is the recommended approach for new languages.

items.description: Block-based WYSIWYG markdown editor (Notion-inspired). The user edits rich formatted content — bold, italic, headings, lists, links, code — with no markdown syntax ever visible. The Value parameter is a raw Markdown string (input and output). Internally each paragraph, heading, or list item is a separate block div; inline formatting uses real semantic HTML elements (<b>, <em>, <s>, <code>, <a>). Supports Ctrl+Enter submit, character limit, link dialog, and keyboard shortcuts (Ctrl+B, Ctrl+I, Ctrl+K).

parameters.name: Class
parameters.description: Additional CSS class applied to the root container element.

parameters.name: IsDisabled
parameters.description: Disables the editor and the entire toolbar.

parameters.name: MaxLength
parameters.description: Maximum number of characters allowed. 0 = unlimited. Shows a character counter in the footer when set.

parameters.name: OnSubmit
parameters.description: Callback fired when the user presses Ctrl+Enter or calls Submit(). Only fires when content is non-empty and within MaxLength.

parameters.name: Placeholder
parameters.description: Placeholder text displayed when the editor is empty.

parameters.name: Value
parameters.description: The markdown content of the editor. Bind this to get/set raw markdown — no HTML.

parameters.name: ValueChanged
parameters.description: Callback fired whenever the markdown content changes.

parameters.name: AdditionalAttributes
parameters.description: Additional HTML attributes applied to the root container via @attributes splatting.

publicMethods.name: GetMarkdown
publicMethods.description: Returns the current raw markdown string. Equivalent to reading the Value parameter.

publicMethods.name: Clear
publicMethods.description: Clears all editor content, resets the character count, and fires ValueChanged with an empty string.

publicMethods.name: Submit
publicMethods.description: Programmatically submits the current content (same as pressing Ctrl+Enter). Fires OnSubmit only when content is non-empty and within MaxLength.

examples.title: Basic usage — bind Value to get raw markdown
examples.code:
@* Live preview *@ 
@_markdown
@code { private string _markdown = string.Empty; }

examples.title: With submit callback and character limit
examples.code:
<TmMarkdownEditor @bind-Value="_comment"
                  Placeholder="Add a comment..."
                  MaxLength="1000"
                  OnSubmit="HandleSubmit" />

@code {
    private string _comment = string.Empty;

    private async Task HandleSubmit()
    {
        await SaveComment(_comment);
        _comment = string.Empty;
    }
}

examples.title: Disabled with pre-filled content
examples.code:
<TmMarkdownEditor Value="@_readonlyContent" IsDisabled="true" />

@code {
    private string _readonlyContent = "# Hello\n\nThis is **read-only** content.";
}

examples.title: Programmatic clear after submit
examples.code:
<TmMarkdownEditor @ref="_editor"
                  @bind-Value="_text"
                  OnSubmit="HandleSubmit" />

@code {
    private TmMarkdownEditor _editor = default!;
    private string _text = string.Empty;

    private async Task HandleSubmit()
    {
        await SaveAsync(_text);
        await _editor.Clear();
    }
}

items.description: Full-featured rich text editor with a comprehensive toolbar supporting headings (H1-H4), text formatting (bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, subscript, superscript), lists (ordered, unordered, task), indentation, links, images, tables, videos, code blocks, blockquotes, horizontal rules, text/highlight colors, emojis, find & replace, @mentions, and {{token}} variable insertion. Provides word count and character limit tracking. Token chips support visual differentiation via Icon, ColorClass, and TypeLabel. Hover over a token chip fires OnTokenHover so the application can display its own tooltip.

items.description: Generic multi-view list supporting Table, Card, and List display modes with a built-in view switcher, search, client-side and server-side grouping with per-group mini-pager, pagination, virtualization, external filter builder, and optional view persistence via IDataTableViewProvider.\n\nComposition rule: either the owning page filters the data and the list renders a content-only surface (set ToolbarMode=ContentOnly and supply pre-filtered Items/DataProvider), or the list owns filtering via its own toolbar and external filter builder. Avoid enabling both filter surfaces at the same time unless they are explicitly integrated.

parameters.name: AllowDrag
parameters.description: When true, selected items can be dragged (e.g. onto a TmTreeView with AllowDrop=true).

parameters.name: AllowSelection
parameters.description: When true, shows checkboxes and enables multi-select mode.

parameters.description: Maps an item to its avatar/thumbnail URL.

parameters.name: CardTemplate
parameters.description: Custom card template. When set, overrides default card rendering.

parameters.name: Class
parameters.description: Additional CSS class for the root element.

parameters.description: Current tenant ID for tenant view scoping.

parameters.name: CurrentUserId
parameters.description: Current user ID for personal view scoping.

parameters.name: DataProvider
parameters.description: Server-side data provider. When set, data is loaded via this provider.

parameters.description: Maps an item to its date value.

parameters.name: DisplayResolver
parameters.description: Universal display resolver for field labels and filter values. DisplayResolver(fieldName, null) → localized field/column label (e.g., "Status" → "Stav") DisplayResolver(fieldName, rawValue) → localized value (e.g., ("Status","Active") → "Aktivní") Return null to use defaults (FilterDefinition.FieldLabel, column Title, or raw value). Set once on the component — flows to ViewManager, FilterBuilder, and ColumnPicker.

items.compositionGuidance: Either the page filters the data, or the list filters the data. When the page owns the filters, use ToolbarMode=ContentOnly and do not set ViewProvider/ExternalFilterDefinitions. When the list owns the filters, use the default Full toolbar mode and optionally a ViewProvider.

               CanCreateTenantViews="true"
               CurrentUserId="@userId"
               CurrentTenantId="@tenantId" />

@code {
    // DisplayResolver flows from TmViewManager → TmFilterBuilder → TmFilterChip.
    // Usually you set DisplayResolver on the parent TmDataTable or TmMultiViewList
    // and it flows automatically. Direct usage shown here for standalone scenarios.
    private string? ResolveDisplay(string fieldName, string? rawValue)
    {
        if (rawValue is null)
            return fieldName switch { "Status" => "Order Status", "Priority" => "Priority", _ => null };
        return (fieldName, rawValue) switch
        {
            ("Status", "Pending") => "Pending",
            ("Status", "Shipped") => "Shipped",
            ("Status", "Delivered") => "Delivered",
            _ => null
        };
    }
}

items.description: Generic form field wrapper providing a label (with optional required marker), help text, error message display, and a slot for any form control. Supports automatic EditContext validation via the ValidationFor parameter — when inside an EditForm, errors from the validation system appear automatically. Applies error styling whenever an error is active (from ErrorMessage or EditContext).

    <input id="username" type="text" @bind="model.Username" />
</TmFormField>

examples.title: Form field with explicit error message
examples.code:
<TmFormField Label="Email" Required="true" ErrorMessage="@emailError">
    <input type="email" @bind="model.Email" />
</TmFormField>

examples.title: Form field with automatic EditContext validation
examples.code:
<EditForm Model="@_model" OnValidSubmit="HandleSubmit">
    <DataAnnotationsValidator />

    <TmFormField Label="Name" Required="true" ValidationFor="@(() => _model.Name)" For="name">
        <TmTextInput id="name" @bind-Value="_model.Name" />
    </TmFormField>

    <TmFormField Label="Age" Required="true" ValidationFor="@(() => _model.Age)">
        <TmNumberInput @bind-Value="_model.Age" Min="0" Max="150" />
    </TmFormField>

    <TmButton Type="ButtonType.Submit">Save</TmButton>
</EditForm>

examples.title: Form field with FluentValidation and automatic errors
examples.code:
<EditForm Model="@_model" OnValidSubmit="HandleSubmit">
    <FluentValidationValidator />

    <TmFormField Label="Department" Required="true" ValidationFor="@(() => _model.Department)">
        <TmSelect TValue="string" @bind-Value="_model.Department"
            Options="@_departmentOptions" Placeholder="Select department" />
    </TmFormField>
</EditForm>

notes: ValidationFor and ErrorMessage can coexist — ErrorMessage always takes precedence when non-empty.
Without ValidationFor the component behaves identically to the original version — fully backward compatible.
Uses Expression<Func<object>> (same as TmFormValidationMessage) so no type parameter is needed at the call site.

examples.description: Implement IIconProvider to provide a whole set of icons (e.g. from a font or sprite sheet). Providers are consulted after the direct registry, in registration order.

notes: Icon names use IconNames constants (e.g. IconNames.Check) to avoid typos.
Edit and Pencil are aliases pointing to the same 'edit' icon.
Custom icons registered via IconRegistry.Register() must contain only inner SVG elements (path, circle, line, etc.) — NOT the <svg> wrapper.
Resolution order: built-in icons → direct registry → registered IIconProvider providers.
If an icon name is not found anywhere, the component renders a <span class='tm-icon-unknown'> fallback.

<TmCascadingSelect TParent="string" TChild="string"
    ParentLabel="Region"
    ChildLabel="City"
    ParentOptions="@_regionOptions"
    ParentPlaceholder="Select region..."
    ChildPlaceholder="Select city..."
    @bind-ParentValue="_region"
    @bind-ChildValue="_city"
    LoadChildOptionsAsync="LoadCitiesAsync" />

@code {
    private string? _region;
    private string? _city;

    private async Task<IReadOnlyList<SelectOption<string>>> LoadCitiesAsync(string? region)
    {
        if (region is null) return [];
        var cities = await _locationService.GetCitiesAsync(region);
        return cities.Select(c => new SelectOption<string>(c.Id, c.Name)).ToList();
    }
}

    @bind-Amount="_amount"
    @bind-Currency="_currency"

    ConvertAsync="ConvertToCzkAsync"

@code {
    private async Task<decimal?> ConvertToCzkAsync(decimal amount, string currency)
    {

    }
}

@code {
    private TmSpreadsheet _spreadsheet = null!;

    private async Task OnFileSelected(InputFileChangeEventArgs e)
    {
        using var stream = e.File.OpenReadStream(5 * 1024 * 1024);
        using var ms = new MemoryStream();
        await stream.CopyToAsync(ms);
        await _spreadsheet.ImportFromExcelAsync(ms.ToArray());
    }

    private async Task ExportAsync()
    {

    }
}

libraryExamples.title: Custom Icon Registration
libraryExamples.description: Register custom application-specific icons via IconRegistry in Program.cs. Icons can be registered individually with inline SVG content, or in bulk via a custom IIconProvider implementation.
libraryExamples.usageCode:
@* Use registered custom icons in Razor — reference by the registered name *@
<TmIcon Name="company-logo" Size="IconSize.Lg" />
<TmIcon Name="app-dashboard" Color="IconColor.Primary" />
<TmIcon Name="app-reports" Size="IconSize.Xl" StrokeWidth="1.5" />
libraryExamples.setupNote: Icon resolution order: built-in icons → direct registry (IconRegistry.Register) → IIconProvider providers (in registration order). SVG content must be inner elements only (path, circle, line, rect, polyline, etc.) — NOT the <svg> wrapper. Names are case-insensitive.

libraryExamples.title: Custom Localization — Full Language Override
libraryExamples.description: Replace all component UI strings with your own translations by implementing ITmLocalizer. Register your implementation AFTER AddTempoBlazor() so TryAddSingleton is skipped. The library has 500+ keys following the Tm[Component]_[Action] naming pattern.
libraryExamples.setupNote: ITmLocalizer is defined in Tempo.Blazor.Abstractions (namespace Tempo.Blazor.Localization). The interface has two indexer overloads: this[string key] for simple lookups and this[string key, params object[] arguments] for formatted strings. Keys follow the pattern Tm[ComponentName]_[Action]. Always return the key itself as fallback for unmapped keys to avoid blank UI. Use string.Format for keys with placeholders like TmDataTable_ShowingItems ({0}–{1} of {2}).

libraryExamples.title: Custom Localization — Partial Override (Decorator)
libraryExamples.description: Override only specific localization strings while keeping the rest from the built-in English/Czech resources. Uses a decorator pattern wrapping the default IStringLocalizer<TmResources>.
libraryExamples.setupNote: This approach injects IStringLocalizer<TmResources> (from the built-in .resx files) into your custom localizer. Only the keys in the _overrides dictionary are changed; everything else comes from the default resources. This works with both English and Czech — the built-in IStringLocalizer respects the current CultureInfo.

libraryExamples.title: Switching UI Language at Runtime
libraryExamples.description: Switch between built-in languages (English, Czech) at runtime using CultureInfo. Tempo.Blazor's DefaultTmLocalizer automatically picks up the culture change.
libraryExamples.setupNote: Built-in languages: 'en' (English, default) and 'cs' (Czech). Set the culture in Program.cs for initial language, or switch at runtime with a page reload. The DefaultTmLocalizer uses IStringLocalizer<TmResources> which respects DefaultThreadCurrentUICulture.

libraryExamples.title: InteractiveAuto Render Mode Setup
libraryExamples.description: Complete setup for Blazor Web App (.NET 8+) with InteractiveAuto rendering, supporting both Server and WebAssembly modes. Tempo.Blazor handles prerendering, double initialization, and JS interop safety automatically.
libraryExamples.setupNote: AddTempoBlazor() registers ITmLocalizer (Singleton), ThemeService (Scoped), and ToastService (Scoped). Call it in both Server and Client Program.cs. Components with JS interop (TmDashboard, TmRichEditor, TmWorkflowDesignerCanvas, TmScheduler) gracefully degrade during prerendering. Multi-targets .NET 8.0, 9.0, and 10.0.

items.description: One rendered wireframe page: its identity and dimensions plus the standalone SVG string.

Produces a clean, interaction-free SVG RenderFragment for a single WireframePage. This is the shared presentation layer reused by the live canvas and by headless server-side rendering (IWireframeSvgRenderer), so the visual stays in one place and previews cannot drift from the editor. It renders ONLY presentation: - the page <svg> root + connector arrow markers (and an optional grid) in <defs>, - the page background, - visible connector paths and their labels, - each element as a translated inner-<svg> viewport hosting the component's WireframeComponentDef.RenderSvg (with a dashed fallback for unknown types). It deliberately omits every piece of interaction chrome: selection/resize handles, connector hit-test paths, waypoint handles, pointer-events surfaces and cursor styling.
Options controlling a static wireframe page → SVG render.

Default IWireframeSvgRenderer built on the static HtmlRenderer. Each render hosts WireframePageSvg.BuildFragment in a tiny throwaway component and serializes the result to a string. No browser, no JS interop — safe to call on the server.

Renders deterministic low-fidelity SVG thumbnails for wireframe documents. The renderer scales the active page into a small SVG, draws each element as a simple rectangle, escapes user-supplied title text, and is suitable for document-library previews outside a Blazor renderer.

R.4.8 / R.5.1 cutover bridge — converts a to/from the JS core-engine model (the { documentId, body: { blocks: [...] } } shape that coreEngine.createCoreEditor consumes). The hosted component (TmDocumentCoreEngineHost) sends to JS and rebuilds the document from on save. R.5.1 — full round-trip (no data loss on save). Round-trips paragraphs, headings, lists, quotes, text runs + inline marks, paragraph alignment, AND the structural blocks that previously vanished: tables (rows/cells/spans/header + nested blocks, recursively), images (standalone ↔ a paragraph carrying a drawing run, plus inline ), and page breaks. Rich C# content the engine does not model (image source/asset/link/natural-size, token/field/note runs) is carried verbatim in a __docSource preserve channel and restored on the way back, with the engine-managed visible fields (text/url/size/wrap/position/caption/alt) overlaid on top so user edits survive.

parameters.description: Raised when the canvas engine reports a model change. This is a plain delegate rather than an ON PURPOSE: it fires on every keystroke, and an EventCallback would auto-invoke StateHasChanged on the (very large) parent editor after every keystroke, re-rendering the whole toolbar/ribbon/chrome and freezing typing. A plain delegate, NOT an EventCallback, for the same reason as : the selection changes on every keystroke (the caret moves), and an EventCallback would auto-render the whole parent editor each time. Pure C# service that recognises Notion-style markdown shortcut patterns typed at the beginning of a block line. Invoke after the user presses Space or Enter. The argument must be the full plain-text content of the current block (including the trigger character that was just appended). Pattern table (most-specific first to avoid prefix collisions): PatternBlock type ### (Space)Heading3 ## (Space)Heading2 # (Space)Heading1 * (Space) or - (Space)BulletList 1. (Space)NumberedList [x] (Space)TodoItem (checked) [] (Space)TodoItem (unchecked) > (Space)Quote ``` (Enter or standalone)Code --- (Enter or standalone)Divider

items.description: Async undo / redo history for a single Notion editor instance. Not a DI service — TmNotionPage creates one instance per page and cascades it to child components via CascadingValue so each page has its own isolated stack. Because provider calls are async the stack exposes async Push / Undo / Redo. The event is raised on every mutation so the UI can refresh without coupling to the stack's internal implementation.

members.description: Begins a new batch scope. All commands pushed while the batch is open will be grouped into a single undo / redo step. Nested batches are not allowed.

members.name: CommitBatch
members.description: Commits the open batch as a single undo step. If the batch contains no commands it is discarded silently.

members.name: PushAsync
members.description: Executes and pushes it onto the undo stack. When a batch is open the command is appended to it instead of being pushed directly — it will be committed as part of .

members.name: RedoAsync
members.description: Re-applies the most recently undone command. No-op when is false.

members.name: RollbackBatchAsync
members.description: Rolls back the open batch: undoes all commands already executed within it and discards the batch without recording it.

members.name: UndoAsync
members.description: Undoes the most recent command. No-op when is false.

Scoped service that centralises all Notion-editor keyboard shortcuts. items.description: Full-featured Notion-style block editor. Supports 20+ block types (paragraphs, headings, lists, code, callouts, toggles, columns, images, video, PDF, file, equation, bookmark, embed, database, diagram, wireframe, spreadsheet), drag-and-drop reordering, slash menu (/), inline formatting toolbar, @@ mentions, [[ page links, {{ token variables, multi-page sidebar navigation, real-time collaboration, comments, page history, import/export, and full keyboard support.

In-process implementation of the document change channel: writers call and subscribers receive for documents they registered via . Suitable for single-process scenarios and as the in-process transport behind a SignalR adapter.

Client-side subscription to document change notifications. A consumer (an open editor, or an embedded block such as a NotionEditor wireframe block) subscribes to the specific documents it displays and refreshes when fires for one of them.
Server-side (or write-side) publication of document change notifications. Invoked after a document is saved, renamed or deleted — by the store, an MCP write tool, or a save flow.

Provides a set of WireframeComponentDef entries to the WireframeComponentRegistry. Built-in Tempo.Blazor components are registered via BuiltInWireframeComponentProvider (priority 0). package.title: Tempo.Reporting.Engine
package.description: Tempo Reporting processing engine with expression evaluation, parameter resolution, layout, snapshots, PDF/PNG rendering, and CSV/XLSX export primitives.

gettingStarted.title: Getting Started with Tempo.Reporting.Engine
gettingStarted.overview: Tempo.Reporting.Engine executes Tempo report definitions: expression evaluation, parameter resolution, data processing, grouping, fixed-page band layout, snapshot generation, PDF/PNG rendering, and CSV/XLSX export.
notes: The engine is pure .NET and can run server-side or in WebAssembly hosts.
Report Server APIs and embedded Blazor report sources use this package for the actual rendering pipeline.
